items.raw_excerpt: A drop-off in foot traffic in Adelaide's CBD prompts an exchange between the state's Property Council and the city council, which are at odds on parking and residential development.
items.summary_en: Fewer people are walking through Adelaide's city centre, according to new council data. The state's property group and the city council are blaming each other over parking and new housing growth in the area.

items.title_en: Adelaide city centre foot traffic drops, councils point fingers

items.raw_excerpt: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has promised to quickly find a new team to operate and reopen two childen's museums being forced to close next week by financial red tape.
items.summary_en: Bangkok City Hall says it will quickly find a new team to run two children's museums. Money rule problems were set to close both places next week. The city wants children to keep visiting them.

items.raw_excerpt: Kiria Tikanah's silver medal is the best result by a Singapore fencer at the Asian Games.

items.raw_excerpt: Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE has released never-before-seen footage of foreign hippies in Ibiza in the early 70s, a film reel censored by Franco’s dictatorship and which showcases how much Spanish society has changed.
items.summary_en: Spain's public broadcaster RTVE has released a film reel that Franco's dictatorship had banned. The film shows foreign hippie life on Ibiza in the early 1970s. Watching it today shows how much Spanish society has changed.

items.raw_excerpt: Moving to the Netherlands means picking not just a country but also a city, and in 2026 that choice matters more than it used to. Rents in the unregulated sector rose 7.3% nationally over the past year, according to the latest Pararius Huurmonitor, pushing the average to roughly €21 per square metre. But that average hides a lot of variation. Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht, The Hague, and Eindhoven, the so-called G5, each behave quite differently right now, and the gap between...
items.summary_en: Rents in the Netherlands rose 7.3 percent in one year to about 21 euros per square meter. Big cities like Amsterdam and Rotterdam each have their own price level, so your city choice matters a lot for your budget.
